sources.title: Pavel Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups (MIT 18.757, complete course lecture notes, 162-page PDF)
sources.locator: Sections 10-13, printed pp. 55-72, read in the complete extracted text: Section 10.6 (complex reflection groups and Theorem 10.6, the Chevalley-Shephard-Todd polynomiality criterion), Section 12.1 (degrees uniquely determined by the invariant Hilbert series 1/prod(1-q^{d_i}); the classical degree lists 2,...,n for A_{n-1}, 2,4,...,2n for B_n and C_n and 2,4,...,2n-2,n for D_n), Proposition 12.1 and Theorem 12.2 (Hilbert-Noether module finiteness, prod d_i = |G|, the coinvariant Hilbert polynomial prod [d_i]_q and the regular-representation clause), Sections 12.3-12.4 and Section 13 (Kostant's theorem).

contents.name: Theorem 10.6: C[V]^G is a polynomial algebra exactly when the faithful finite G is generated by complex reflections
Section 10.6 list of complex reflection groups, including the dihedral groups, S_n on C^{n-1} and the exceptional Coxeter groups H_3,H_4,F_4,E_6,E_7,E_8
Proposition 12.1(i): the monic orbit polynomial prod_{g in G}(x-ga) of each coordinate has invariant coefficients, so each coordinate is algebraic over the invariant field
Section 12.1: the invariant Hilbert series 1/prod(1-q^{d_i}) uniquely determines the degrees
Section 12.1: classical degree lists for A_{n-1}, B_n, C_n and D_n
Theorem 12.2: prod_i d_i = |G| and the coinvariant Hilbert polynomial prod_i [d_i]_q
Sections 12.1-12.2: the Hilbert series of the invariants, matched against the Molien trace sum
Theorem 12.2, regular-representation clause: the coinvariant algebra is the regular representation
contents.reason: The page proves only the degree sums, the discriminant identity and the top sign line; the source report requires an exact-character supplier for the regular-representation strengthening, and this pair deliberately does not build one.

contents.name: Proposition 12.1(ii) and the Artin-Tate module-finiteness argument
contents.reason: Module finiteness is not needed here: the n-generator count and algebraic independence come from the published invariant-theory suppliers, and the orbit annihilator alone gives the algebraicity used by the Jacobian lemma.

contents.name: Section 13, Kostant's theorem for symmetric algebras of Lie algebras
contents.reason: Lie-theoretic harmonic decompositions are the proof home of finite-weyl-invariants-bruhat-and-kostant-harmonics and are explicitly not identified with the Coxeter coinvariant algebra on this page.

sources.title: Bill Casselman, Essays on Coxeter groups: Coxeter elements in finite Coxeter groups (author-hosted lecture notes, 12-page PDF)
sources.locator: Introduction, Sections 1-4 and the table on printed p. 11, read in the complete extracted text. The introduction records the essay's incompleteness: it does not discuss the order formula in terms of the number of roots and does not treat the relation between eigenvalues of Coxeter elements and polynomial invariants of W.

contents.name: Section 1: the Coxeter element as the product of the generators in a special (bipartite) numbering, and the symmetric positive definite matrix A with 2A the Cartan matrix
Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 3.2: no Coxeter element has eigenvalue 1
Propositions 3.4 and 3.7: the -1 eigenspace and the bijection between eigenvalue pairs of the Coxeter element and eigenvalues of the Cartan matrix
contents.reason: The pair uses only the residues of c and its Coxeter plane, never the Cartan-matrix eigenvalue correspondence, so this stronger spectral comparison is not imported.

contents.name: Theorem 3.11: the Coxeter element acts on its invariant plane as a rotation through 2 pi/h
Table on printed p. 11 of Coxeter numbers h for A_n, C_n, D_n and E_6,E_7,E_8,F_4,G_2
Section 2, icosahedron example: the H_3 Coxeter element has eigenvalues e^{2 pi i/10}, -1 and e^{-2 pi i/10}
Introduction's explicit statement of the two topics the essay does not treat (order formula from the number of roots; eigenvalues versus invariants)
contents.reason: Recorded as a reading limit: precisely those two facts are proved locally on this page, namely that the residue sum equals n h/2 and that the degrees equal one plus the exponents, and they are not attributed to this source.

sources.title: Josh Swanson, On eigenvalues of representations of reflection groups and wreath products (University of Washington CAT seminar notes, 7-page PDF)
sources.locator: Lecture 1, pp. 1-4, read in the complete extracted text: Definitions 1, 6, 9, 14 and 17, Theorems 7, 11 and 15, Remark 10, and the statements of Theorems 20, 33 and 43-45.

contents.name: Definition 1: cyclic exponents of an element of finite order, with diagonalisability in characteristic zero
Theorem 7 (Chevalley-Shephard-Todd equivalence) and Definitions 6, 9, 14 (reflections, degrees, coinvariant algebra)
Theorem 11 (Coxeter): the degrees of a finite Coxeter group are one plus the exponents, all Coxeter elements being conjugate
Remark 10: the product of the degrees is the group order and the coinvariant Poincare polynomial is the product of the q-analogues
Theorem 15 (Chevalley): the coinvariant algebra is isomorphic to the regular representation
contents.reason: This strengthening needs character-theoretic input that this pair does not build, and the source report forbids inferring it from the dimension alone; only the top-degree sign line is proved here.

contents.name: Theorem 20 (Springer), Example 21 and Theorems 33, 43-45 (fake degrees, the Shephard-Todd classification and Specht/Stembridge wreath-product character theory)
contents.reason: The general regular-element and fake-degree machinery, the complex-reflection classification and wreath-product character theory belong to other pages; this pair uses only the Coxeter classification, the regular eigenvector of the bipartite Coxeter element and explicit dihedral computations.

sources.title: Vivien Ripoll (Strobl seminar notes, joint work with Reiner and Stump), Coxeter elements in well-generated reflection groups (57-page PDF)
sources.locator: Slides 1-4 and slide 25, read in the complete extracted text: the absolute-order/noncrossing context, the W-Catalan number prod (d_i+h)/d_i, and slide 25 with the facts h=d_n, the c-stable plane with rotation angle 2 pi/h, and the Springer regular-element conjugacy statement.

contents.name: Slide 25: h equals the highest invariant degree d_n and c acts as a rotation of angle 2 pi/h on a stable plane, hence has eigenvalue e^{2 pi i/h}
Slide 25, Springer theory clause: the elements with eigenvalue e^{2 pi i/h} form one conjugacy class, and c is a Coxeter element iff it has that eigenvalue
contents.reason: The conjugacy-class and characterization clauses are not needed: this page works with the explicit bipartite Coxeter element and its Coxeter plane from the local enumeration, and imports no regular-element classification.

contents.name: Slide 4: the W-Catalan number Cat(W) = prod_i (d_i+h)/d_i
contents.reason: The W-Catalan cardinality product is a separate enumeration theorem, explicitly excluded by the noncrossing scaffold and the current batch31 coverage. The approved noncrossing items prove the lattice, conjugacy independence, Kreweras map and type-A partition model; the invariant-degree theorem here does not by itself prove general NC(W) counting. No approved pair promises this product.
